home.name: Jun Kai
home.aboutMe: Most of what I build starts where something else stopped: a benchmark someone set, or a problem taken as solved until you measure it. Curiosity mostly, with a competitive streak. Professionally that's full-stack product engineering, with deeper specialisation in Rust numerical computing, security tooling and uncertainty quantification.

kipo.description: Built much of the web application and the platform systems beneath it, through the scale-up from stealth to ~1,000 active users over a 2M+ component index.
kipo.bullet1: Rewrote the authentication and session system to unblock OAuth and enterprise rollout, with cross-browser end-to-end tests guarding the flow.
kipo.bullet2: Rebuilt the product's real-time core on Temporal, replacing a WebSocket-and-SSE patchwork and in-process state, and split chat from search — opening product directions the original coupling had ruled out.
kipo.bullet3: Rebuilt the deploy pipeline and test suite over several sprints — unit, end-to-end and fuzz, with the front-end tests driven through the accessibility layer — which surfaced and closed a backlog of latent defects.

dsbj.description: Internal platform work for an electronics manufacturer — making complex models readable to the domain experts who rely on them, and unifying login across six applications.
dsbj.bullet1: Built a model visualisation platform with LLM-based diagnostics, used day to day by the domain experts who had to interpret the models.
dsbj.bullet2: Replaced six independently built authentication systems with one — modern password hashing, proper access and refresh tokens, and consistent session management across all six applications.

ai4x.title: Quantifying Uncertainty in Physics-Informed Neural Networks
ai4x.description: Deep evidential regression applied to PINNs — a way to tell when a prediction should not be trusted. Demonstrated on Burgers and Laplace.
ai4x.abstract: We integrate a state-of-the-art method to quantify aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties in physics-informed neural networks and observe that they can be captured effectively while maintaining predictive accuracy.

pyvolr.name: pyvolr
pyvolr.description: A Python library for Black-Scholes-Merton and Black-76 pricing, all five Greeks, and implied volatility — fully vectorised over NumPy and drop-in compatible with `py_vollib`/`vollib`.
pyvolr.bullet1: Fastest in the active BSM ecosystem at scale: 1M implied-vol solves run ~2× faster than fast-vollib’s numba backend and ~12× faster than opengreeks, and 1M strikes price in ~4 ms — on a Rust core exposed via PyO3, parallelised with rayon, and still sub-microsecond on scalar input.
pyvolr.bullet2: Stays f64-exact down to option prices of 1e-215, where fast-vollib, opengreeks and quantforge all begin returning silently-wrong constants — Jäckel’s “Let’s Be Rational” solver over an `erfcx`-based normal CDF, pinned against an mpmath golden ladder and differential-tested in CI.
pyvolr.bullet3: Wheels for Python 3.10–3.14 across Linux, macOS and Windows, including free-threaded 3.13t and 3.14t builds, published through PyPI Trusted Publishing with no stored credentials — plus `py_vollib` and `py_vollib_vectorized` shims that migrate existing users in one import line.

secretsSpotter.name: Secrets Spotter
secretsSpotter.description: An open-source CLI and Chrome extension that detects exposed secrets in files, directories, stdin, web pages, and network traffic — powered by a shared Rust core.
secretsSpotter.bullet1: Built a unified Rust detection engine with 60+ patterns (AWS, GitHub, Stripe, JWTs, private keys, and more) plus false-positive filtering via Shannon entropy, character-class diversity, and code-identifier rejection — shared across the CLI and browser extension from a single core.
secretsSpotter.bullet2: Shipped a CI/CD-ready CLI with SARIF output for GitHub Code Scanning, JSON mode for automation, and glob and severity filters.
secretsSpotter.bullet3: Engineered a WASM-powered Chrome extension that scans DOM content and intercepts fetch, XHR, WebSocket, SSE, and cookies through a MAIN-world interceptor, with SHA-256 deduplication and automatic re-scan on SPA navigations — all fully local.
